A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same GraphRAG-Bench research. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, tables, rendered figures, and embedded prompts, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original generation, retrieval, graph-structure, and token-cost results on the Novel and Medical datasets, including experiments with GPT-4o-mini and Qwen2.5-14B.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds results for further comparison methods and quantitative task-complexity analyses.

M1.justification: The six-stage benchmark-construction procedure, GPT-4.1-assisted ontology extraction and refinement, and question-generation prompts are retained. Appendix A.3 explains complexity control more explicitly without establishing a changed construction algorithm. Additional evaluated frameworks are comparators, not newly proposed methods.

E1.justification: Evaluation retains the Novel and Medical datasets and the same four task categories. v2 Appendix D proposes future legal and financial extensions and supplies corpus inventories, but reports no training or task evaluation in those domains.

E2.justification: v2 Tables 9–10 add evaluated Lazy-GraphRAG, KGP, StructRAG, and KET-RAG comparisons across both datasets. These were previously cited rather than evaluated. Microsoft GraphRAG's local/global variants remain present in the appendices under MS-GraphRAG naming, and the Qwen2.5-14B comparator set is unchanged.

E3.justification: Context relevance changes from averaging two normalized ratings in v1 Equation 3 to averaging relevance judgments over retrieved contexts using the question and reference evidence in v2 Appendix F. Table 8 also introduces triple-count and inference-hop measurements. The generation backbones and previously stated configurations remain unchanged; rerunning the retained experiments is not established.

E4.justification: v2 Appendix A.3 and Table 8 add a focused analysis of knowledge breadth and reasoning depth across task categories in both datasets. This quantifies the claimed complexity distinctions. The existing corpus-connectivity analysis and Qwen2.5-14B evaluation are retained rather than newly added.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. The new descriptive complexity statistics do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v2 adds extensive results for four comparators, complexity measurements, corpus inventories, and previously missing medical MS-GraphRAG(global) entries. RAPTOR's medical creative-generation faithfulness changes from 58.98 in v1 Table 8 to 59.98 in v2 Table 9. Table 2 replaces its entity values with statistics already present in v1's appendix, including UltraDomain's 8.23 becoming 170.6. The Qwen2.5-14B results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equation 3 substantively redefines context relevance: the mean of two discrete ratings becomes a mean of per-context relevance judgments involving the question and reference evidence. This is more than relocating an equation to Appendix F. The remaining graph-quality, recall, and generation formulas are retained; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contribution: a benchmark combining contrasting corpus structures, four complexity categories, and evaluation across graph construction, retrieval, and generation to investigate when GraphRAG helps. The added evidence does not redefine these headline claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds an argument that question format does not determine retrieval or reasoning difficulty, explicitly qualifies that more graph relationships need not improve performance, and discusses legal/financial extension requirements, including numerical-data processing. The earlier retrieval trade-offs and text-only limitation remain.

D1.justification: Appendix H.2 newly specifies 256-token chunks for basic RAG, without establishing that chunking changed. Table 15 expands implementation descriptions for the added comparators. The new Reproducibility Statement reports original-data release and an additional anonymous repository, while FAQ A.1 narrows the described GitHub scripts from preprocessing/construction/training/evaluation to evaluation.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to existing benchmarks, Han et al.'s analysis, and DIGIMON remain substantively unchanged. The newly evaluated comparators were already cited in v1. Author–year citation conversion, reference reordering, and an added ArchRAG URL do not introduce new research positioning.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section ordering are retained. v2 makes localized wording, terminology, and author-information edits; expands the FAQs; inserts takeaway and domain-extension sections; adds ethics, reproducibility, and LLM-use statements; and moves retrieval equations into the appendix.

P2.justification: v2 adds a leaderboard screenshot and guidance infographic (Figures 6–7), complexity and corpus-inventory tables (Tables 8 and 12), and substantially expands comparison and implementation tables. Main-text result selection, typography, captions, and placements also change. The original scientific plots and prompt graphics are retained unchanged.

improvement.justification: The broader comparator evaluation, explicit complexity measurements, additional implementation details, and reconciliation of Table 2 with the appendix modestly improve empirical coverage and inspectability. The gains are limited by reporting problems: the changed relevance definition is not reconciled with retained scores, Observation 7 newly claims higher HippoRAG2 recall despite Table 4, and Figure 6 disagrees with Table 9 on KGP's medical fact-retrieval accuracy.
